title: Safety factor sensitivity & mitigation scenarios — GPU capacity modeling (Sep 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a sensitivity-focused approach to setting spare capacity (safety factors) across regions and GPU families. Goal is to produce a small set of defensible safety-factor recommendations (per-region, per-GPU-family) plus mitigations for common failure/surge modes. This is intentionally exploratory — contains provisional numbers and TODOs for follow-up data runs.

Assumptions (base):
- Regions considered: us-west1, us-east1, europe-west1, asia-southeast1.
- GPU families in active fleet: H100-80GB, A100-40GB, T4 (inference-critical legacy).
- Baseline traffic model uses 30-day rolling p50/p95 token-throughput converted to GPU-equivalents using the model-mix profile from /analytics/served-models (linked).
- Cold-start and model-compile spikes are treated as transient surges (10-15% additional peak for up to 5 minutes).
- Recovery window target: 10 minutes for region-level re-provisioning (auto-scaling + cross-region warm pool).

Key inputs (columns for the sheet):
- Region
- GPU_family
- Active_pool (GPUs)
- Typical_peak_p50 (GPU-equivalents)
- Typical_peak_p95 (GPU-equivalents)
- Observed_AZ_loss_impact (pct of capacity lost when an AZ fails)
- Transit_fallback_impact (added latency / cost if routed)
- Cost_per_hour_per_GPU (USD)
- Target_safety_factor (decimal, e.g., 0.25 = 25% spare)
- Required_spare (GPUs) [calculated]
- Notes / mitigations

Sample rows (provisional numbers for sensitivity runs):
Region,GPU_family,Active_pool,Peak_p50,Peak_p95,AZ_loss_impact,Cost_per_hour,Target_safety_factor,Required_spare,Notes
us-west1,H100,480,360,420,33%,6.50,0.20,96,"Warm pool in us-west2 = 40 GPUs; prioritize H100 migrations; can fallback to A100 (perf delta +5%)"
us-east1,A100,320,240,300,25%,4.50,0.18,58,"Higher traffic variance during EMEA off-hours; keep 2 hot nodes per AZ"
europe-west1,H100,160,120,150,34%,6.80,0.30,48,"Regulatory: private nodes reserved for enterprise tenants; separate accounting"
asia-southeast1,A100,120,90,110,50%,5.00,0.25,30,"Higher AZ fragility historically; consider stronger safety factor"

Formulas (how Required_spare derived):
- baseline_required = max(0, Peak_p95 - Active_pool * (1 - AZ_loss_impact))
- required_spare = ceil(baseline_required + Peak_p95 * Target_safety_factor)
Notes: this lumps AZ loss and safety factor; we test alternatives (apply safety factor first then subtract AZ loss) in sensitivity runs.

Sensitivity analysis plan (short):
1) Deterministic scenarios: vary Target_safety_factor = [0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.50] and observe regional shortfall counts.
2) AZ-outage scenarios: simulate single AZ down (apply AZ_loss_impact) and double-AZ within region (if applicable).
3) Cross-region outage: remove entire region and test routing absorption capacity (assumes warm pools in neighboring region are available).
4) Monte Carlo daily-variation: run 10k sims sampling peak demand from empirical distribution (p10..p99) and AZ failure probability (0.5%–2% daily). Compute expected unmet-GPU-hours and 99th-percentile unmet.
5) Cost/benefit: compute incremental $/GPU-hour for each extra spare target and cost per avoided downtime-minute using historical failure severity.

Preliminary outputs (sensitivity highlights):
- Small safety factors (10%) lead to acceptable day-to-day variance but expose us to >2 minute median failover pain for AZ loss in large regions (us-west1).
- 30% safety factor materially reduces probability of unmet demand in simulated surge+AZ cases (p99 unmet goes to ~0.2% regionally) but increases hourly cost by ~12% on active fleet.
- asia-southeast1 requires the highest safety factor by raw shortfall numbers due to historically higher AZ instability; a hybrid mitigation (stronger local safety factor + instant cross-region warm routing) gives better cost efficiency than pure local spares.

Mitigation ladder (recommended operational controls, prioritized):
1) Fast warm pool spin-up (1–3 minutes) in region-pair: maintain minimal compile-ready images and locked kernels.
2) Staged fallback to compatible GPU family with quantization-aware model variants (A100 <- H100 fallback path).
3) Traffic shedding policies for non-critical / bulk workloads (background embedding jobs) during recovery window.
4) Dynamic safety factor ramp: increase regional safety factor automatically when anomaly detectors detect increasing request variance.
5) Reserve contractual burst capacity with cloud partner for region-wide emergency (limit: 200 GPU-hours per incident).

Runbook excerpt (for SRE on-call):
- Incident: Region AZ outage (single AZ with 30% capacity gone)
  1) Confirm scope: metrics + infra alerts (loss of N nodes).
  2) Activate warm-pool in neighboring AZ/region (runbook command: infra/warm-pool/trigger us-west2 H100 40).
  3) Shift non-enterprise traffic to lower-cost quantized model in fallback cluster (tag: fallback-quantized-v2).
  4) Notify product + CS: ETA for full recovery estimated by autoscale logs.
  5) Post-incident: run the sensitivity script (sheet ID linked) to recompute safety factors and surface cost delta.

Appendix — quick sensitivity snapshot (p95 unmet GPUs by safety factor):
Region: us-west1 — safety_factor 0.10 -> p95_unmet 9 GPUs; 0.20 -> p95_unmet 4 GPUs; 0.30 -> p95_unmet 1 GPU
Region: us-east1 — safety_factor 0.10 -> p95_unmet 7 GPUs; 0.20 -> 2 GPUs; 0.30 -> 0 GPUs
Region: europe-west1 — safety_factor 0.10 -> 3 GPUs; 0.20 -> 1 GPU; 0.30 -> 0 GPUs
Region: asia-southeast1 — safety_factor 0.10 -> 12 GPUs; 0.20 -> 6 GPUs; 0.30 -> 2 GPUs

Notes to reviewer: this doc is a synthesis of initial runs and product constraints. The active workbook in spreadsheets has the full per-minute simulation output (link above). Prefer to converge on a single-page policy: per-region baseline safety factor + a conditional routing policy for cross-region burst.
